integrity: Conditioning a fixed vertex to have indegree zero leaves the restriction to all other vertices as an iid uniform mapping on n-1 labels, while the conditioned vertex cannot be cyclic. The stochastic comparison is proved from an exact cyclic-point tail law obtained by rooted-forest enumeration. An exhaustive checker independently replays the identities through n=7.
scientific_limitations: The deletion identity uses the fully uniform random-mapping law and need not persist for general exchangeable-indegree models.
The result concerns cyclic-core size and its transforms, not full negative association of fringe and core statistics.
The cyclic-point marginal law is classical; the claimed contribution is the explicit zero-indegree Palm deletion law and its dependence consequences.
title: Empty-indegree Palm deletion forces negative cyclic-core dependence
